title: Stack & Ingestion Health
description: Platform-side health: what the ingestion daemon is landing in the historian, and how the hypertable and its rollups are growing. Reads only objects that exist on the HISTORIAN -- `gateways` and `asset_config` live in Supabase and were queried here by mistake, which is why those panels are gone rather than fixed.

panels.title: Telemetry Rows Ingested (per second)
panels.description: Rows landing in the `telemetry` hypertable, bucketed at one minute. This is the historian-side view of ingestion throughput. The daemon's own drop counters are NOT here and are a different question: this counts what was WRITTEN, and `Messages Dropped by Reason` below counts what was refused. A fall here with no rise there is a quiet plant; a fall here WITH a rise there is a fault.

targets.rawSql:
SELECT time_bucket('1 minute', time) AS "time",
       'rows/sec' AS metric,
       count(*) / 60.0 AS value
  FROM telemetry
 WHERE $__timeFilter(time)
 GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY 1

panels.title: Ingestion Rate by Device
panels.description: Per-device write rate. Under report-by-exception a flat line at zero is a device whose values are not moving, NOT a device that has stopped -- absence and steadiness are the same signal here, which is what the 5-minute keepalive bounds.

targets.rawSql:
SELECT time_bucket('1 minute', t.time) AS "time",
       coalesce(a.asset_name, t.asset_id) AS metric,
       count(*) AS value
  FROM telemetry t LEFT JOIN assets a ON a.asset_id = t.asset_id
 WHERE $__timeFilter(t.time)
 GROUP BY 1, 2 ORDER BY 1

panels.title: Active Series
panels.description: Distinct (device, metric) pairs with a sample in the window. Bounded by series count rather than by history, which is the property `telemetry_latest` exists for.

targets.rawSql:
SELECT now() AS "time", 'series' AS metric,
       count(*)::float AS value
  FROM (SELECT DISTINCT asset_id, metric_name FROM telemetry
         WHERE $__timeFilter(time)) s

panels.title: Devices Reporting
panels.description: Distinct devices with a sample in the window.

targets.rawSql:
SELECT now() AS "time", 'devices' AS metric,
       count(DISTINCT asset_id)::float AS value
  FROM telemetry WHERE $__timeFilter(time)

panels.title: Rows in Hypertable
panels.description: Total raw observations retained. Raw is dropped on the retention policy while the rollups outlive it -- that split is deliberate and is what lets a question about last spring be answered at all.

targets.rawSql:
SELECT now() AS "time", 'rows' AS metric, count(*)::float AS value
  FROM telemetry

panels.title: Messages Dropped by Reason
panels.description:
Messages the daemon REFUSED, by reason, from `acs_ingestion_messages_dropped_total`. This is telemetry that was not recorded and will not be restated.

THIS PANEL IS HALF AN INSTRUMENT. The counter says a drop happened and how many; it cannot say WHICH DEVICE, under which edge node, because the metrics endpoint is served without a credential and carries no device data of any kind by design. That half is in the log store -- click any series to open it filtered to the same reason.

The two halves cannot disagree: `drop("<reason>")` in ingestion.py derives the Prometheus label and the logged field from one string, and ingestion/test_structured_logging.py asserts they stay identical.

THE LINK SELECTS ON `service="ingestion"`. The chart's Alloy applies that label; an external log stack must relabel `service` to the workload name or this link returns nothing.

links.title: Which devices? Open the logs for this reason

panels.title: Rollup Bucket Coverage
panels.description: Buckets materialised in each rollup. The hierarchy is 1m -> 5m -> 1h, each built from the one before, so a gap that appears only in the coarser views is a refresh policy problem rather than an ingestion one.

targets.rawSql:
SELECT bucket AS "time", '1 minute' AS metric, count(*) AS value
  FROM telemetry_1m WHERE $__timeFilter(bucket) GROUP BY 1
 UNION ALL
SELECT bucket, '5 minute', count(*) FROM telemetry_5m
 WHERE $__timeFilter(bucket) GROUP BY 1
 UNION ALL
SELECT bucket, '1 hour', count(*) FROM telemetry_1h
 WHERE $__timeFilter(bucket) GROUP BY 1
 ORDER BY 1

panels.title: Historian I/O by Backend
panels.description: From pg_stat_io. `grafana_reader` holds pg_monitor, which grants visibility into the statistics views and nothing else.

targets.rawSql:
SELECT backend_type AS "Backend", object AS "Object",
       context AS "Context", hits AS "Cache hits", reads AS "Disk reads"
  FROM pg_stat_io
 WHERE hits > 0 OR reads > 0
 ORDER BY reads DESC NULLS LAST LIMIT 20

panels.title: Total Stored
panels.description: Every byte this platform holds, across both databases: the historian's hypertables and rollups over postgres_fdw, plus the Supabase public schema locally. Table, index and TOAST included.

panels.title: Audit Trail (never pruned)
panels.description: public.digital_thread. THE ONE RELATION HERE WITH NO RETENTION POLICY BY DESIGN -- it is append-only to every application role and migration 0003 blocks UPDATE and DELETE, so this number only ever rises. Watching it is the point of separating it from `metadata`.

targets.rawSql:
SELECT total_bytes AS "Audit" FROM public.storage_footprint
 WHERE source = 'platform' AND relation = 'digital_thread'

panels.title: Raw Telemetry Compression
panels.description: Bytes after compression as a fraction of before, for the raw hypertable. Empty in TWO cases and they are not the same: TIMESCALE_COMPRESS_AFTER is 'never', or the policy is on and no chunk has aged past it yet. hypertable_compression_stats() reports NULL for both, so storage_footprint passes NULL through rather than inventing a zero -- 'compressed to nothing' and 'nothing compressed' must not render alike.

targets.rawSql:
SELECT compressed_bytes::numeric / NULLIF(uncompressed_bytes, 0) AS "Ratio"
  FROM public.storage_footprint
 WHERE tier = 'raw' AND uncompressed_bytes IS NOT NULL

panels.title: Raw Retention Horizon
panels.description: How far back the raw hypertable's chunks reach. Read from chunk BOUNDARIES in the catalog, not from min(time) -- a storage dashboard must not be the reason for a full scan of the historian. Should track TIMESCALE_RETAIN_FOR; a horizon well past it means the retention policy is not running.

targets.rawSql:
SELECT EXTRACT(EPOCH FROM (now() - oldest_data)) AS "Age"
  FROM public.storage_footprint WHERE tier = 'raw'

panels.title: Storage by Tier
panels.description: Where the bytes are. 'Total stored is 4 GB' tells an operator nothing they can act on; '3.6 GB is raw telemetry retention will drop, 300 MB is an audit trail nothing will ever drop' tells them what to do next.

targets.rawSql:
SELECT tier AS "Tier", sum(total_bytes) AS "Bytes"
  FROM public.storage_footprint
 GROUP BY tier
 ORDER BY sum(total_bytes) DESC

panels.title: Relations by Size
panels.description: Every relation, both databases, largest first. `chunks` and the compression columns are empty for platform tables because those are hypertable concepts -- NULL rather than zero, since a plain table is not 'compressed to nothing', it is one the question does not apply to. `collected_at` advancing is what proves the FDW read is live rather than a cached foreign scan.

targets.rawSql:
SELECT source        AS "Database",
       tier          AS "Tier",
       relation      AS "Relation",
       total_bytes   AS "Total",
       table_bytes   AS "Table",
       index_bytes   AS "Index",
       chunks        AS "Chunks",
       oldest_data   AS "Oldest"
  FROM public.storage_footprint
 ORDER BY total_bytes DESC
